---
title: "Back up and restore the shop's data"
subtitle: "SOP SYS-08 · Technical systems manual"
---

## Purpose

Save a copy of everything the shop has recorded, so it can be put back if the
computer fails, the database storage is deleted, or a change goes wrong.

## Applies to

The person responsible for the shop's database: at the end of each day the
shop is open, before any change to the app or to Docker, and whenever the
shop's data must be put back.

## Before you begin

- The shop's app is running. See [SYS-03 Start, stop and check the shop's
  app](start-the-app.qmd).

## What a backup holds

A backup is one file, named with the date and time it was made, such as
`shop-backup-2026-10-16_20-50-55.zip`. The time is in UTC (Greenwich time),
so it can differ from the shop's clock by several hours. Every backup is
kept in the `backups` folder inside the `dog-groomer-platform` folder.

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| `grooming_demo` | The shop app's database: every client, dog, booking, haircut, allergy and paperwork record entered in the shop's screens |
| `grooming_test` | The test database. See [SYS-07](reset-databases.qmd) |
| `private/` | Every file in the `private` folder: the copies of paperwork and the dog photos that the records point to |

::: {.callout-important}
## A backup holds real clients' details
The file holds names, phone numbers, vaccine paperwork and photos. Keep
every copy of it as carefully as the paperwork itself. The `backups` folder
is never published to GitHub.
:::

## Procedure

### Make a backup

1. Open the Technical workbench at <http://localhost:8501>.
2. In the left menu, click **Run & test**.
3. Click the **Database** tab.
4. Scroll down to **Backups**, at the bottom of the tab.
5. Click **Back up now**. The output appears below the button. It finishes
   with **Backup saved:** and the name of the new file. Nothing in the shop's
   data is changed.

### Keep a copy away from this computer

A backup on this computer is lost if the computer is lost. Once a week, and
after any large change:

6. Open File Explorer.
7. Open the `dog-groomer-platform` folder, then the `backups` folder.
8. Copy the newest file to a USB drive kept away from the computer. The
   newest file is the one with the latest date and time in its name.

### Restore a backup

Restoring replaces the shop's data with the copy in the backup. Everything
recorded in the shop's screens since that backup was made is replaced.
Before it replaces anything, the restore saves a backup of what is there
now, so a restore can itself be undone.

9. Open the Technical workbench at <http://localhost:8501>.
10. In the left menu, click **Run & test**.
11. Click the **Database** tab.
12. Scroll down to **Backups**, at the bottom of the tab.
13. Click the **Backup to restore** list, below the **Back up now** button.
    The backups appear, newest first.
14. Click the backup to restore.
15. Click **Restore this backup…**. A box opens that says what will be
    replaced.
16. Click **Yes, restore it**. The output appears below. It finishes with
    **Restored from** and the name of the backup.
17. Open <http://localhost:3000>, or reload it if it is already open. The
    shop's screens show the data as it was when the backup was made.

To restore a backup from a USB drive, first copy the file into the
`backups` folder, then follow steps 9 to 17.

### Do the same from a terminal instead

The same commands, without the Technical workbench. Open a terminal in the
`dog-groomer-platform` folder.

- To make a backup, type this command and press Enter:

  ```bash
  docker compose exec review python shop_backup.py save
  ```

- To see the backups, newest first, type this command and press Enter:

  ```bash
  docker compose exec review python shop_backup.py list
  ```

- To restore the newest backup, type this command and press Enter:

  ```bash
  docker compose exec review python shop_backup.py restore
  ```

  The command says what it will replace, then asks **Type yes to restore**.
  Type `yes` and press Enter to restore. Type anything else to stop without
  changing anything.

- To restore an older backup, type its name after `restore`, for example:

  ```bash
  docker compose exec review python shop_backup.py restore shop-backup-2026-10-16_20-50-55.zip
  ```

## Result

After a backup, the `backups` folder holds a new file with the date and time
in its name. After a restore, the shop's screens show the clients, dogs,
bookings and photos exactly as they were when that backup was made.

## If something goes wrong

### Stopped: cannot reach the database

The app is not running. Start it (see [SYS-03](start-the-app.qmd)), then
repeat the procedure.

### Stopped: the backup's grooming_demo would not load. The shop's data was not changed.

The backup file is damaged or incomplete. The shop's data is exactly as it
was before the restore. Choose an older backup and restore that instead.

### Stopped: there are no backups in backups/ to restore.

The `backups` folder is empty. If a backup is on a USB drive, copy it into
the `backups` folder first.

### The wrong backup was restored

Every restore first saves what was there, in a file whose name ends in
`before-restore`. Restore that file to undo the restore: in step 14, click
the newest file ending in `before-restore`.

### The database storage was deleted

This happens after `docker compose down -v`. Start the app (see
[SYS-03](start-the-app.qmd)). On the first start it builds a fresh demo
database holding only the made-up demo dogs. Then restore the newest backup, following steps 9 to 17. If the
`backups` folder was lost with the computer, copy the newest backup from the
USB drive into it first.
